```java
    public String submit(String line) {
        String verb = "???", date = "????-??-??";
        try {
            InstructionParser.Parsed p = parser.parse(line);
            verb = p.verb(); date = p.date();
            String res = switch (verb) {
                case "TRANSFER" -> engine.transfer(date, p.fields()[2], p.fields()[3], new BigDecimal(p.fields()[4]).setScale(2), p.fields()[5]);
                case "WITHDRAW" -> engine.withdraw(date, p.fields()[2], new BigDecimal(p.fields()[3]).setScale(2));
                case "DEPOSIT" -> engine.deposit(date, p.fields()[2], new BigDecimal(p.fields()[3]).setScale(2));
                case "REVERSE" -> engine.reverse(date, p.fields()[2]);
                default -> "REJECTED BAD_INSTRUCTION: unknown verb " + verb;
            };
            if (res.startsWith("REJECTED")) return reject(verb, date, res);
            if (res.contains("TX-")) {
                rs.recordOk(date);
                aus.record(verb, date, res.substring(0, res.indexOf(" fee=")));
                return res;
            }
            return res;
        } catch (InstructionParser.ParseException e) {
            return reject(verb, date, "REJECTED " + e.code + ": " + e.message);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return reject(verb, date, "REJECTED BAD_AMOUNT: " + (line != null ? line : "null"));
        }
    }
```

The `catch (Exception e)` block is too broad. When `new BigDecimal(p.fields()[4])` fails, it throws `NumberFormatException`, which is caught by `Exception e`. The `reject` method then produces `REJECTED BAD_AMOUNT: [full line]`.
The tests expect `REJECTED BAD_AMOUNT: 0` (just the value), not the whole line.

The line `res.substring(res.indexOf(" REJECTED") + 9, res.indexOf(":"))` is probably failing or returning wrong strings because `res.indexOf(" REJECTED")` might be -1.

```java
    public BigDecimal parseAmount(String val) {
        if (val == null || !val.matches("\\d+(\\.\\d{1,2})?")) throw new ParseException("BAD_AMOUNT", val);
```
